label: Out-of-Office Party Keeps Prohibition
detail: The party out of the presidency since 1921 drops its call for repeal and stands behind the national ban on alcohol.
assumption: The Democratic nominee and platform back continued Prohibition rather than repeal, so wet voters lose their main reason to prefer him while dry voters see the two major tickets as alike on liquor.
facts_text: The party out of the presidency since 1921 has dropped its call for repeal of the Eighteenth Amendment from its platform.
Both major parties now stand for keeping the national ban on alcohol.
nominee_news: He announced that he would keep the national ban on alcohol and would not support its repeal.
Editors have noted that he has broken with those in his party who demand an end to the liquor ban.

add_planks.text: Support continued enforcement of the Eighteenth Amendment and oppose its repeal.

research_questions: How did wet urban voters behave in 1928 when neither major party offered repeal?
How much did the repeal issue move voters toward the party out of power in 1932?
Did dry rural Protestants stay with the party in office when both parties were dry?
